To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effectiveness of enforcement is affected by the financial status of the firm being enforced and that, when the firm’s financial status is taken into consideration, increased enforcement may actually reduce abatement, rather than increase abatement as conventional wisdom holds.

1) financial dimensions are important for understanding the effect of enforcement, 2) the impact of enforcement depends on the financial dimension considered, 3) the impact of the likelihood of enforcement on abatement is nonmonotonic and depends on financial constraints, and 4) increased likelihood of enforcement can lead to worse environmental outcomes when financial status is taken into account.

the effectiveness of environmental regulation is influenced by the financial status of firms, that the effectiveness of enforcement depends on both the probability of enforcement and the severity of the sanctions imposed, and that the conventional wisdom regarding enforcement likelihood and abatement is only correct when the financial status of the regulated firm is not considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between the financial constraints of firms and enforcement policy.
the role that corporate financial status plays in influencing the effectiveness of environmental regulations, which is a topic that has received very little attention to date.
how financial constraints influence the effectiveness of environmental policy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
enforcement can improve environmental performance, but the impact of enforcement is sensitive to the financial status of regulated firms.
the financial status of regulated firms can have a significant influence on both the effectiveness and the efficiency of enforcement.
enforcement can improve environmental performance, but only when it is combined with a proper consideration of the firms' financial status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interactions between enforcement, corporate financial status and environmental performance are complex and that the effectiveness of environmental policy depends crucially on the interactions among these factors.
financial constraints can have important implications for the effectiveness of environmental regulation.
the effectiveness of environmental regulation depends not only on the design of the regulatory program, but also on the financial status of the regulated firm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enforcement policy should be designed in a way that takes into consideration firms’ financial constraints.
the effectiveness of enforcement depends critically on the financial status of the firms being regulated.
enforcement policy needs to be tailored to the financial status of firms in the industry.
